This numb, shut-down feeling has been creeping in since the first year after my husband passed, and it's been going on almost every single day for a little over two years now.\n\nDoctor: During this time, have you also been feeling depressed or hopeless most days, or is it mainly a sense of grief and missing your husband?\n\nPatient: It doesn't really feel like active sadness or hopelessness, and it's different from just missing my husband. I just don't have any drive or ability to care about the things I used to love anymore.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any changes in your sleep, appetite, energy, or concentration since this started? I’m trying to tell whether this is more like depression or a grief-related reaction.\n\nPatient: My energy is completely gone, like a switch was turned off, and I barely manage to eat simple meals. It's just this heavy, overwhelming emptiness that makes it impossible to do anything.\n\nDoctor: When you think about your husband, do you mainly feel longing and sadness about the loss, or do you feel persistently depressed, worthless, or guilty most days?\n\nPatient: I don't really feel guilty or worthless, and it's not even a sharp longing anymore. It is just a persistent, heavy numbness, like a switch was turned off inside me and left me completely empty.
